KS-senate.statusNote: Sen. Roger Marshall (R) faces Rev. Adam Hamilton (D), pastor of the largest Methodist church in the U.S., nominated Aug 4.

KS-governor.statusNote: Open seat (Gov. Kelly term-limited): Senate President Ty Masterson (R) faces state Sen. Cindy Holscher (D). Both nominated Aug 4.

candidates.name: Ty Masterson
candidates.background: President of the Kansas Senate; state senator since 2009 after service in the Kansas House and on the Andover City Council. Former realtor and construction small-business owner. Won the Aug 4 Republican primary with 43% in a seven-candidate field; endorsed by President Trump.

cost.label: Frames affordability through tax cuts ('Kansas taxes too much'); pledges utility-ratepayer protections on data centers (campaign site)

health.label: Opposes Medicaid expansion; led the Senate where expansion was defeated 12-28 (Kansas Reflector)

immigration.label: SB 452 ('Halo Act') expanding protections for ICE and federal agents was introduced at his urging; passed Senate 31-7 (Kansas Reflector)

taxes.label: Touts leading a ~$2B tax cut and promises more: 'Kansas taxes too much and delivers too little' (campaign site)

education.label: Raise pay for 'good teachers', put parents in charge, hold spending accountable; banned DEI in higher ed (campaign site)

safety.label: 'Fund the police and fight for safer streets'; cites 24% public-safety budget increase (campaign site)

repro.label: Anti-abortion; linked electing Supreme Court justices to ending Kansas abortion-rights protections (Kansas Reflector)

democracy.label: Pledges 'commonsense measures to protect the ballot box' (campaign site)

climate.label: Pledges to be 'the most oil and gas friendly governor this state has seen' and is 'super engaged with ethanol' (KCTV5)

controversies.label: Criticized over his 2025 vote for 20-year data-center tax breaks and for pressuring the state bank commissioner on behalf of Beneficient, whose CEO was later convicted of fraud (Kansas Reflector)

nullNotes.housing: checked campaign site, KCTV5 economy interview, and GOP debate coverage; laments first-time homebuyer age over 40 but no housing policy mechanism documented

candidates.name: Cindy Holscher
candidates.background: Kansas state senator since 2021, previously a state representative (2017-2020); spent about 12 years in marketing at Sprint before politics. Won the Aug 4 Democratic primary 49-39 over Ethan Corson, who had Gov. Kelly's endorsement.
priorities: Moratorium on new hyperscale data centers

cost.label: $16 minimum wage, paid sick time, tax-free diapers and hygiene products, cut costs on 'healthcare, childcare, groceries, and gas' (campaign site)

health.label: Expand Medicaid to low- and moderate-income Kansans; legalize medical marijuana to lower costs (campaign site)

housing.label: Build more affordable housing, cap late-rent penalties, cut the residential property assessment rate (campaign site)

immigration.label: Opposes ICE raids and detention expansion; will 'pull every lever as governor to protect our neighbors' (Democracy Now)

education.label: Fully fund all classrooms, free school lunch for every student, expand special-education funding (campaign site)

repro.label: Supports abortion rights; called the judicial-election amendment a 'backdoor attempt' to undermine reproductive health care (Democracy Now)

democracy.label: Independent redistricting panel, term limits, limits on corporate PAC money (campaign site)

taxes.label: Attacks 'continued giveaways to billionaires and corporations, which leaves regular people behind'; would end data-center tax incentives (Democracy Now)

nullNotes.climate: checked campaign priorities page, Democracy Now interview, and KCTV5 interview; data-center moratorium is a utility and water-use stance, no clean-energy versus fossil position documented
nullNotes.safety: checked campaign priorities page and Democracy Now interview, nothing documented

candidates.name: Roger Marshall
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2021; OB-GYN physician; previously represented Kansas's Big First district in the House.

health.label: Opposes 'Obamacare' and 'socialized medicine'; voted to repeal the individual mandate (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Supports the border wall; 'turn off the magnets' attracting migrants (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: 'The less control the federal government has, the better off we will be', lower taxes, less regulation (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Opposes EPA Waters of the U.S. rules and environmental regulation of farming (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: 'Life begins at conception'; backed Heartbeat Bill, 20-week ban, defunding Planned Parenthood (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Objected to certifying Arizona and Pennsylvania 2020 electoral votes (Ballotpedia)

cost.label: Lower cost of living through price transparency and competition (Patients Deserve Price Tags Act) and cutting regulations, not price caps (Senate office)

housing.label: Mixed: co-sponsored the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act expanding the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, while blaming 'the regulatory environment' for driving up home-building costs (Senate office)

education.label: Lead sponsor of the Educational Choice for Children Act, $10B a year in scholarship tax credits: 'Parents, not the government, know what is best for their children' (Senate office)

safety.label: His Concerned Citizens Bill of Rights blocks DOJ COPS and Byrne grants from jurisdictions with cashless bail or that ignore 'criminal history and dangerousness' pretrial (Senate office)

candidates.name: Adam Hamilton
candidates.background: Founding pastor of the Church of the Resurrection, the largest United Methodist congregation in the U.S.; first-time candidate running as an 'independent-minded Democrat.' Won the Aug 4 primary.

cost.label: Critical of tariffs as a cost to consumers (Christian Post platform coverage)

repro.label: 'Pro-choice on abortion', platform statement, no further detail yet (Christian Post)

health.label: 'Reverse the cuts to Medicaid and restore the ACA subsidies'; expand Medicare drug-price negotiation and add vision and dental (campaign issues)

housing.label: 'Ban Wall St. and other investors from buying up single family homes', first-time buyer tax credits, stop landlord algorithmic price collusion; also streamline modular-home rules (campaign issues)

immigration.label: Reform the H-2A guest-worker program with year-round visas and 'give existing workers a path to legal status' (campaign issues)

climate.label: Mixed, cost-framed: 'stop the war on domestic energy projects and restore energy production tax credits', year-round E15 ethanol, and make data centers 'pay their fair share of electricity costs' (campaign issues)

democracy.label: Term limits and age limits for Congress and the Supreme Court, end 'dark money', congressional stock-trading ban, lobbying cooling-off periods (campaign issues)

nullNotes.taxes: checked campaign issues page and Christian Post platform coverage; no position on tax rates or spending documented
nullNotes.education: checked campaign issues page and Christian Post platform coverage, nothing documented
nullNotes.safety: checked campaign issues page and Christian Post platform coverage, nothing documented
